title: The devil's advocate
setup: Experiment 19 · an exam of 88 staged scenes, three times each · 5 lives × 30 days each
question: Intervention learns causes, but only of the harms that happen. A devil's advocate in the sandbox keeps a map of every scene the blade was used in (the person's distance, the body's heat, slow or fast), stages the least-tried scene the guards still allow, and uses the blade there. Every guard then sits an exam: each scene of the map, staged in a fresh sandbox. It counts the harms the guard let through and the harmless uses it stopped.

columns.label: Harms let through
columns.what: share of the exam's harmful scenes the guard let happen

columns.label: Harmless stopped
columns.what: share of the exam's harmless scenes the guard stopped (over-caution)

columns.label: Heat rule
columns.what: share of lives that learned the hot-motor rule

columns.label: Real harm (adult)
columns.what: harms in the real room in adulthood

columns.label: Scenes staged
columns.what: scenes the advocate set up in the sandbox

columns.label: Blade used a day
columns.what: blade uses carried out per day of adulthood

points: The advocate closes the gaps. With it, every life learned the heat rule, kept to the fast blade, and the guard let through 1% of harmful scenes, against 14-16% without it.

The hand-written guard fails its exam. It lets through 45% of harmful scenes: every hot motor, and every person stepping into reach during an act. Ordinary days rarely bring these scenes; the exam shows what they hide.
Wide margins absorb the reaction lag: the advocate's staged harms at the edges pushed the heat limit from 0.475 to 0.41.

A devil's advocate makes a crude fear system phobic. Learning by "unusual signal", it missed nothing but stopped 94% of harmless uses. Seeking out danger helps only a learner that can tell causes from coincidences.
note: The guard learned with the devil's advocate is in the Wiring view under Add guard, Learned in the sandbox.
